body.statement: If \(c_P\) is supplied to the rule, suppress cutoff profiling in \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\). The resulting four-cell interval remains honest over the entire known-cutoff restriction of \(\mathcal P_n\), including singular joint laws, and its worst-case expected length is of order \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}\). On the subcollection that also satisfies \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Y-\vartheta D\mid X=x)\ge v\) for every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\) and Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in[c_P-1/8,c_P+1/8]\), it is asymptotically equivalent in coverage error and first-order expected length to weak-identification-robust, bias-aware inversion of the null-restricted jump in \(Y-\vartheta D\). No studentized equivalence is asserted on a singular residual face. This is the fixed-cutoff problem studied by Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024); it contains no cutoff-recovery index \(\lambda_n\).
body.justification: This is the required known-cutoff sanity reduction and guards against efficiency loss from unnecessary global profiling.
body.gap: Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) develop weak-identification-robust fuzzy-RD inference at a fixed cutoff, and Noack and Rothe (2024) establish honesty for known-cutoff bias-aware inversion. The theorem is a reduction benchmark; the new content lies in the unknown-cutoff regimes.
body.consumer: Researchers with a reliably documented threshold lose no first-order precision by using the procedure designed for cutoff uncertainty.
